_description: Architectural decision records: routing, state management, build pipeline, major library choices, cross-cutting refactors. Append only; supersede with a new entry instead of editing.

title: Pin TypeScript to 6.0
decision: Pin typescript to the 6.0 line in package.json.
rationale: volar (vue-tsc) and typescript-eslint do not support TS 7 yet.
consequences_negative: Must revisit when tooling supports TS 7.

title: Proxy all GitHub API calls through Nitro with the user OAuth token
context: The app reads and writes the user's GitHub repos from a client-only SPA.
decision: Every GitHub call goes through server/routes/gh-*; the handler reads the token from the nuxt-auth-utils secure session and forwards it as Bearer.
rationale: Secure session data stays server-side, so the GitHub token never reaches the browser; owner is forced to the session user.
consequences_positive: No token in client JS; per-user isolation; zod validation at one trust boundary.
consequences_negative: A Nitro server is required at runtime, so a purely static deploy is not possible.

title: Build the folder layout on Nuxt UI dashboard components
context: The redesign (direction A, 'Finder') needs a persistent vault sidebar, a single header and a mobile drawer for the folder view.
decision: src/layouts/default.vue uses UDashboardGroup + UDashboardSidebar + UDashboardPanel + UDashboardNavbar; vaults render through UNavigationMenu in VaultNavigation.vue.
rationale: Nuxt UI 4 already ships these components with responsive drawer, toggle and theming, so no hand-written shell or extra dependency is needed.
consequences_positive: Sidebar collapse, mobile drawer and spacing come from the library; layout code shrinks.
consequences_negative: Layout markup is tied to Nuxt UI dashboard slots; a library major upgrade may require rework.

title: Detect vault repos by the gitvault GitHub topic, not a marker file
context: Vaults were detected by the gitvault- name prefix, which forces repo names. plan/05 proposed the topic plus a .gitvault marker file in the repo root.
decision: A repo is a vault iff it has the gitvault topic or (transition) the gitvault- name prefix (isVaultRepo in server/resources/gitHubUserRepos.ts). Creation sets the topic with PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/topics right after POST /user/repos. No marker file.
rationale: GET /user/repos already returns topics, so detection costs zero extra calls; a marker file would need a contents/tree call per repo on every list. The prefix fallback keeps existing untagged vaults working without a migration.
consequences_positive: Repo names can become free once the naming UI drops the prefix; no extra API calls on list.
consequences_negative: Creating a vault takes two GitHub calls and can half-fail (repo created, not tagged); the error names the repo. Removing the topic on GitHub hides a non-prefixed vault. The prefix fallback must be removed deliberately later.

title: Phone backup dedupes by blob sha against the repo tree
context: Users want to back up a phone gallery by re-picking it whole each time, uploading only what is new. Phone file names and dates are unreliable (renames, iOS export dates, IMG_0001 reused across phones).
decision: The backup page (src/pages/[repo]/backup.vue) hashes each picked file client-side as a git blob (sha-1 of 'blob <size>\0' + bytes), skips files whose sha appears anywhere in the gh-repo-tree listing, and queues the rest on the shared useVaultContents upload queue under Photos/YYYY/MM from file.lastModified, with keepBoth: content is known to be new, so a name clash is a different photo and is saved as 'name (n).ext' without asking. Files over MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (src/config.ts) are skipped and listed.
rationale: The tree already carries every blob sha in one request, so dedupe needs no index file, no extra GitHub calls and no new dependency, and it survives renames and moves inside the vault. Reusing the queue keeps one upload pipeline (conflict handling, serial PUTs).
consequences_positive: Re-selecting the whole gallery only uploads new items; moved or renamed files still count as backed up.
consequences_negative: Every file is read fully in memory to hash; a truncated tree (very large repos) misses shas, so an already stored photo with the same name can be saved again as 'name (n).ext'. The size cap follows the proxy: the base64 body must fit Netlify's function request limit, so large videos are skipped. The /<repo>/backup route shadows a root folder named backup.

title: Vaults are identified only by the gitvault topic; the gitvault- name prefix is removed
context: After the gitvault topic became the vault marker, the client still prepended gitvault- to new repo names, stripped it again for display (getVaultLabel) and isVaultRepo still accepted untagged gitvault-* repos as legacy vaults.
decision: New vaults are created with the name as typed (trimmed). GITVAULT_REPO_PREFIX and getVaultLabel are deleted; isVaultRepo checks the topic only and the UI shows the repo name as-is. No backward compatibility: existing gitvault-* repos were tagged with the topic by hand.
rationale: One marker instead of two; the prefix added nothing the user sees and made repo names diverge from vault names.
consequences_negative: A vault name can collide with an existing repo of the user (GitHub 422), including the auto-created 'personal'
An untagged gitvault-* repo is no longer a vault; it must get the gitvault topic to show up
Old vaults keep the gitvault- prefix in their visible name unless renamed on GitHub

title: OAuth requests the delete_repo scope so vaults can be deleted from the app
context: Deleting a vault means deleting its GitHub repo, which GitHub only allows with the delete_repo OAuth scope; the app requested repo only.
decision: The GitHub OAuth handler requests repo and delete_repo. Sessions without delete_repo get GitHub's 403, shown as a plain error toast: the app had no users when the scope was added, so no dedicated re-login hint was built. The server deletes only repos that carry the gitvault topic and are owned by the session user.
rationale: No other way to delete a repo through the API. Because the token can now delete any repo of the user, the vault check is enforced server-side, not trusted from the client, and the UI asks for the vault name typed out before deleting.
consequences_positive: Users can delete a vault without leaving the app
consequences_negative: Every existing session must sign in again before deleting a vault
The token is more powerful: a bug in the server guard could delete a non-vault repo
The consent screen asks for a broader permission

title: Rename a file with one Git Data API commit, not contents PUT + DELETE
context: GitHub has no rename endpoint. The contents API would need PUT at the new path then DELETE at the old one.
decision: PATCH gh-repo-contents (server/utils/renameFile.ts) commits through commitTreeChanges (server/utils/commitTreeChanges.ts, shared with folder delete): from the recursive tree of the branch head it checks the old entry (regular file with the sha the user saw, else vaultChanged; symlink/submodule/folder: notRenamable) and that the new path is free (else nameTaken), then writes the same blob and mode at the new path and drops the old one; a non-fast-forward ref update is retried once on the new head. Same folder only, extension locked (the client edits the base name, the server rejects a changed extension). Error codes travel in the error's data.code and the client translates them.
rationale: One atomic commit; the content is not re-sent through the proxy, so no base64 overhead and no request body size limit; a fast-forward-only ref update never loses a concurrent commit. The tree gives the entry mode and type, which the contents API hides (it follows symlinks), and is not capped at 1,000 entries per folder. A locked extension keeps previews and the replace picker working.
consequences_positive: Works for files of any size
A failure leaves the repo untouched (never two copies or none)
Executable bits survive; symlinks are refused instead of turned into files
consequences_negative: Five GitHub calls per rename, one of them the whole recursive tree
A vault whose tree GitHub truncates (about 100,000 entries) can't rename
Changing a file's extension needs a re-upload

title: Public landing at /, app under /vaults, only / server-rendered
context: GitVault needs a public, SEO-indexable landing page, but the app is a client-only SPA (ssr: false) whose pages sat at / and /<repo>.
decision: / is the landing for everyone (logged in or not), prerendered at build via routeRules ('/**': ssr false, '/': ssr true + prerender). All vault pages move under /vaults (getVaultUrl adds the prefix). /login becomes a routeRules redirect to /vaults; 00.auth sends anonymous users to / and the OAuth success redirect goes to /vaults. The 01.guest middleware is removed.
rationale: Prerendered HTML gives crawlers the full content with no server render cost and is served from the CDN; keeping every app route client-only avoids making the vault code SSR-safe. A route rule can only disable SSR, so the global ssr: false had to go. A dedicated /vaults prefix keeps app URLs from colliding with landing/marketing paths and lets robots.txt disallow the app in one line. Sending anonymous users to / (not /login) avoids a redirect loop now that /login points into the app.
consequences_positive: Landing is indexable and fast (static file)
App behaviour unchanged apart from URLs
consequences_negative: Code reachable from / must be SSR-safe
The landing renders the logged-out state first and switches after the client session fetch
